body:
PR946's proposed encoding changes alter bytes authenticated by historical packages. The batch952 review already identified eight PR950 conflicts; this research consolidation adds an exact wider inventory and executable evidence for preserving the historical source closure. **No new kappa; no approval or application of PR946.**

- Scans all 10,707 regular JSON files at base `407d52ff15b2217b6e22bce44728b4c3907b6515`, with zero parse failures. The closed literal-record grammar finds 561 old-byte references across 99 files and 148 proposed paths, plus 330 proposed-byte and 42 other-digest records. These counts are provenance references, not claims of 561 runtime failures.
- Binds all 165 proposed paths to PR946 head `b6e22dbf548d72f18b722ccb6c2ea8e3d9df6ac1`, its actual parent `91a2094f2e022930069e8cfdc810a3ea1b81cd09`, the retained maintainer inventory, and a direct Git diff/blob check.
- The unchanged PR950 verifier rejects each of its eight proposed inputs independently. Restoring seven scripts while retaining the proposed certificate still fails. Restoring all eight reproduces the complete 6,760,000-coefficient historical audit and original receipt `ffae0f0a22863718e3134a924592dcf4b05e919223323ba536c587c592bfe6a1`, with all 46 closure files unchanged. No expected digest is relaxed.
- Records five additional literal source references in the later accepted PR970 package. No new PR970 runtime replay is claimed.

Only `research/pr946-pin-migration/` is added: verifier, reproducible inventory, eight exact proposed-byte fixtures, execution receipt, scope/migration guidance, local sprint claim and attribution. Production code, `upstream/`, selected certificates and frontier stay unchanged.

Validation (Windows, Python 3.14.5, standard library):

```sh
python -I -B research/pr946-pin-migration/check.py
```

Expected final marker: `PASS_PR946_PIN_MIGRATION ... single_file_rejections=8 full_audits=2 coefficients_per_audit=6760000 kappa=unchanged`. Also passed `--check-proposal`, six adversarial inventory tests normally and under `-O`, the selected-record checker, and staged fixture SHA256 checks. Full replay deliberately requires assertions. The separate agent review independently checked all JSON parsing and found no provenance bypass; it is not human peer review. No Linux CI or repository-wide `make verify` result is claimed.

Seed **95**, research-consolidation track. No pinned coordination issue was present; the local claim is completed with its result link. Before submission, upstream refreshed to `8bddbee377e2f3ce1f1247196c4b290d55767d20`; the proposal head, selected kappa, and PR950 input/adapter hashes were unchanged. Targeted overlap searches and latest open PRs through #986 found no matching migration contribution; this was not an exhaustive census.

Credits: Aaron Wang/navinor (#946), Ross Richardson (#950), Douglas R. Colkitt and the original verifier lineage, the batch952 maintainers for the original conflict finding, and predecessor reproducibility work named in `NOTICE.md`. Prepared for **woklerx with substantial OpenAI Codex AI assistance**. Apache-2.0. General dependency discovery, migration of every consumer, the broad encoding integration, and inherited multiplication-theorem obligations remain outside this contribution.
title: Research consolidation: PR946 frozen-pin inventory and restoration replay (no new kappa)
